name: Philip's four daughters (prophetesses)
title: The Four Prophetesses from Caesarea
summary: Philip's four daughters were unmarried women who had the gift of prophecy. They lived with their father, the evangelist Philip, in Caesarea and represent an important recognition of women's prophetic ministry in the early church.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as prophetesses
keyEvents.description: Luke describes that Philip had four unmarried daughters who had the gift of prophecy, showing that women held recognized spiritual gifts in the early church.

keyEvents.title: Paul visits their home
keyEvents.description: The apostle Paul and his traveling companions stayed with Philip and his family in Caesarea on the way to Jerusalem, thus meeting the four prophetesses.

keyEvents.title: Part of a prophetic environment
keyEvents.description: During Paul's stay, the prophet Agabus also came to Caesarea and prophesied about Paul's fate, showing the active prophetic environment the daughters were part of.

keyEvents.title: Fulfillment of Joel's prophecy
keyEvents.description: Their prophetic gift can be seen as a fulfillment of the prophecy that God's Spirit would be poured out on all people, and that sons and daughters would prophesy.
